title: On the Impact of Extra Information in Bandit Learning: More is Not Always Merrier
author: Ramakrishnan Krishnamurthy
snippet: More data is commonly assumed to improve learning performance, however, we show that this intuition can surprisngly fail in sequential decision-making. Considering a stochastic bandits setup with exogenous extra information, we ask if the free and unbiased extra reward samples…
excerpt: More data is commonly assumed to improve learning performance, however, we show that this intuition can surprisngly fail in sequential decision-making. Considering a stochastic bandits setup with exogenous extra information, we ask if the free and unbiased extra reward samples are guaranteed to reduce the regret of the learner. We introduce a formal notion of `non-degradation under extra information' and demonstrate that the widely used Upper Confidence Bound algorithm (UCB) violates this property, i.e., there exist benign extra-information under which UCB incurs strictly higher regret than when run without extra information. We contrast this behaviour with Thompson Sampling and Explore-Then-Commit, which appear to benefit from the same extra information. Constructively, we propose a meta-algorithm that provably enforces non-degradation for a broad class of bandit algorithms. We also run empirical simulations to study our meta-algorithm.
